summary: This standards-track memo updates the required and suggested algorithms for Internet Key Exchange version 1. The original specification allowed weak security and suggested algorithms that were rarely implemented, so this document aligns it with market needs.

plainLanguage.summary: An old rulebook for secret handshakes listed weak methods. This document updates the list to better ones.

questions: which diffie-hellman group is mandatory in ikev1
what does rfc 4109 change in rfc 2409
subtitle: Replaces the old must-support algorithm list for IKEv1 with one that drops weak choices and adds AES.

tldr.problem: The algorithm requirements in the original IKEv1 specification allowed weak security and suggested algorithms that were thinly implemented.
tldr.mechanism: This memo changes the MUST and SHOULD levels in RFC 2409: TripleDES, SHA-1, pre-shared secrets and Diffie-Hellman group 2 become MUST, AES-128 in CBC mode and group 14 become SHOULD, and weak or unused algorithms drop to MAY.
tldr.outcome: Implementers of IKEv1 get a requirement list that matches the IPsec market, and the memo predicts AES-128 in CBC mode will become mandatory if IKEv1 is updated again.

today: RFC 4109 is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 2409. No later RFC obsoletes it.

sections.title: Why Update RFC 2409
sections.content: The original IKEv1 definition, RFC 2409, has MUST-level and SHOULD-level requirements that do not match the needs of IPsec users. This document updates it by changing the algorithm requirements, and it is intended for all IKEv1 implementations deployed today.
sections.plainLanguage: The old list of required tools no longer matched what people needed, so this document rewrites it.

sections.title: Old and New Requirements
sections.content:
Under RFC 2409, DES for encryption, MD5 and SHA-1 for hashing, pre-shared secrets and Diffie-Hellman MODP group 1 (768 bits) were MUST. TripleDES, Tiger, DSA and RSA signatures, RSA encryption and MODP group 2 (1024 bits) were SHOULD. RFC 2409 also gave conflicting levels for elliptic-curve groups.

The new MUST list is TripleDES for encryption, SHA-1 for hashing and HMAC, pre-shared secrets, and Diffie-Hellman MODP group 2 (1024 bits). The new SHOULD list is AES-128 in CBC mode, AES-128 in XCBC mode for PRF functions, MODP group 14 (2048 bits) and RSA for signatures.
sections.plainLanguage: The new list says which locks every handshake must know, and which extra, stronger locks it should know.

sections.title: What Was Dropped and Why
sections.content:
DES, MD5 and MODP group 1 drop to MAY because of cryptographic weakness. Tiger, elliptic-curve MODP groups, DSA signatures and RSA with encryption drop to MAY because of a lack of significant deployment and interoperability.

The memo also says that if more updates to IKEv1 are made, AES-128 in CBC mode will very likely become mandatory.
sections.plainLanguage: Some old tools were weak, and others almost nobody used. Both kinds were moved to 'optional'.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says the whole document is about security. All the algorithms at MUST or SHOULD level in the new requirements are believed to be robust and secure at the time of writing.
sections.plainLanguage: The tools on the new required list were thought to be strong when it was written.
